subject: Novara Health: rapid on-prem feasibility — scope, runway, resourcing
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18 09:12 PDT
Subject: Novara Health pilot — rapid on‑prem feasibility (initial ask)

Olga / Karthik / Steph,

Novara (contact: Ana Morales) pinged us this morning asking whether we can run a tightly scoped on‑prem pilot inside their VPC (air‑gapped-ish) with a 6‑week runway. High level asks from them:

- Private control plane (customer-managed network) or a restricted egress model
- Customer key management (KMS integration) and no token logs sent externally
- Ability to receive model updates via offline bundle (they will not allow direct model pulls)
- Target: ~50–100 qps peak for inference, 10k tokens/day typical; burst to 300 rps during batch jobs
- Expected go/no‑go decision in ~4 weeks, pilot in ~6 weeks if we greenlight

They flagged SOC2 evidence and an audit window as gating. Ana said procurement will likely ask for an exception lane for standard Private offering (timeline + dedicated eng support).

Can we do a quick triage here: what are the minimal runtime/ops staffing assumptions we need to commit to for a 6‑week pilot? Also note: they explicitly asked for a signed runbook and oncall commitment for the pilot duration.

Attaching their initial requirements PDF that Ana sent. If this is feasible I think we should propose a constrained scope (single model, pinned version, no streaming) and a clear backstop if we need to fall back to hosted.

Thanks — can we get an initial thumbs up/no from arch + ops by EOD Monday so we can schedule a customer readout on Tuesday?

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Product Manager, Private Hosting
Redwood Inference

Attachment: novara_requirements_v1.pdf

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18 11:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Novara Health pilot — rapid on‑prem feasibility (initial ask)

Grace — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the PDF. Quick clarifying questions before I block the triage slot:

1) Data residency: do they require model artifacts to never leave their environment, or are we allowed to ship model bundles once (offline)?
2) SLA expectations: what latency SLOs do they expect for 50–100 qps? (p95 token latency target?)
3) Security: KMS provider preference? HSM requirement?
4) Ops runway: do they expect Redwood engineers on‑site or remote support only?

From an initial look, the big integration blockers are packaging a stable runtime bundle + handling offline model updates and key management. If Karthik can give a short feasibility note (rough list of missing infra pieces and minimal FTE per week), we can scope a workback and owners.

I can host a 60m triage on Monday 10/19 10:00 PT if that works for everyone — will invite Novara.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Integrations (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

From: Ana Morales <ana.morales@novarahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18 14:45 PDT
Subject: Re: Novara Health pilot — rapid on‑prem feasibility (initial ask)

Thanks Grace — quick answers from our side to Olga's questions:

1) Model artifacts: must remain in our network. We can accept an initial model bundle (signed tarball) delivered via SFTP delivered to our staging host; no outbound model pulls allowed.
2) Latency: p95 inference time target = 220ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens). Throughput target is as above (50–100 qps steady, tolerate bursts).
3) KMS: we use AWS KMS + CloudHSM for root keys; HSM may be optional but KMS integration is mandatory.
4) Support: remote support is fine; no on‑site required up front. We will expect scheduled weekly syncs and a documented incident contact (pager on call).

I attached the internal security checklist we will share with procurement and auditor teams. We aim for an internal decision on the pilot by 11/15.

— Ana Morales
VP, Infrastructure — Novara Health

Attachment: novara_requirements_v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19 08:07 PDT
Subject: Re: Novara Health pilot — rapid on‑prem feasibility (initial ask)

On Mon, Oct 19, 2026 at 08:07 AM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Olga: can we get a short feasibility note

Quick triage summary from runtime/ops perspective (short form):

- Packaging: feasible via a runtime bundle (docker + precompiled kernels) delivered as an offline artifact. We need a signed checksum and SFTP process. (Blocker: automated model pull flows must be disabled for pilot.)
- KMS: integration with AWS KMS for key unwrap is straightforward if Novara exposes a keywrap endpoint or grants decrypt privileges to a bootstrap VM. CloudHSM for root keys will require additional coordination (1–2 sprint effort).
- Networking: customer requires no outbound model fetching; we need a one‑way telemetry channel design (or none). Telemetry: default telemetry must be opt‑out for this pilot.
- Staffing: minimal support posture — 0.5 FTE/week runtime engineer + 0.2 FTE security engineer for onboarding + 0.1 FTE product throughout the pilot. For incident response we need a named oncall with a max 4hr SLA during business hours (pilot only).
- Ops runbook: we can produce a slim runbook in ~5 working days if we get required infra details.

Primary unknowns that will change scope: audit evidence packaging (SOC2 artifacts), HSM provisioning timeline, and whether Novara wants streaming generations (we should disallow for initial pilot).

Attaching quick notes.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: onprem-runtime-fit-notes.md

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ana Morales <ana.morales@novarahealth.com>, procurement@novarahealth.com (Rob Chen)
Date: 2026-10-20 15:48 PDT
Subject: Re: Novara Health pilot — rapid on‑prem feasibility (initial ask)

Thanks all for the fast turnaround. Summary and proposed next steps:

Summary assessment (green): packaging + offline model bundle, KMS integration (AWS KMS) as long as Novara can provide decrypt privileges to a bootstrap host, and a slim runbook are feasible within the requested window. Primary risk: CloudHSM requirement (if insisted) could add 3–6 weeks.

Proposed constrained pilot scope (what we commit to):
- Single model, pinned version delivered as signed artifact
- No streaming, no external telemetry by default
- Remote support only; named oncall with 4hr weekday SLA
- Deliverables: slim runbook, installation checklist, and acceptance test suite

Owners & resourcing ask (decision needed):
- Runtime engineering lead: Karthik Iyer (0.5 FTE/week) — APPROVE?
- Security liaison: Stephanie Nguyen (0.2 FTE/week) — APPROVE?
- Product owner: Grace O'Connor (0.1 FTE/week) — APPROVE?
- Program manager (onboarding / procurement lane): Olga Petrov (0.1 FTE/week)

If leadership approves this exception lane we will: (1) confirm procurement terms with Novara, (2) schedule a 60m onboarding sync next Tues 10/26, and (3) start producing the slim runbook (target v0 in 5 business days).

Please reply with explicit APPROVE / HOLD / REJECT for the staffing commits and whether we should sign the pilot work under the standard Private contract with an exceptions appendix. Grace — I will draft the appendix once staffing is agreed.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Integrations (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
